title: Micro-adjudication queue heuristics journal
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad for small-scale adjudication queue rules that we can iterate on before formalizing in Confluence. This is intentionally sparse — notes-to-self, examples, and tiny heuristics we can convert into triage scripts later.

Context: micro-adjudication = cases that fail majority consensus or automated voting and are routed to single human adjudicator instead of full pair-adjudication. Goal is to keep latency < 24h and minimize adjudicator cognitive load.

High-level policy ideas (first pass):
- Auto-assign to micro-adjudicator when: label disagreement between >=3 annotators and confidence stdev > 0.22, and example length < 400 chars. (Long examples go to pair adjudication.)
- Fast-pass if disagreement is only about formatting (e.g., punctuation/spaces) -> auto-normalize and close.
- If disagreement is about entity span boundaries and both spans overlap >50% -> adjudicate by picking the longer span unless it captures stopwords only.
- If disagreement is about label taxon (e.g., ORG vs PRODUCT) and surface form matches known gazetteer with high precision -> favor gazetteer label, else escalate.

Example edge cases to capture in heuristics: 
- Short ambiguous tokens like "Acme" appearing in product-descriptor contexts ("Acme 2.0"). Rule: if preceding token is an adjective or number and frequency of labeling as PRODUCT in the last 30d > 0.6 -> label PRODUCT.
- Email-like tokens inside free text: when token contains '@' treat as CONTACT unless annotator majority disagrees; if disagreement, micro-adjudicate but prefer CONTACT.
- Hyphenated compound tokens: prefer single span if hyphen connects words with lexical head on left.

Adjudication micro-protocol (practical):
1) Read 3 annotator notes + their short justification (we already capture those in UI).
2) Check quick context (±40 chars). If all three mention the same rationale but different span offsets -> normalize span to contain non-whitespace boundary and close.
3) If rationale differs, pick label that preserves downstream evaluation stability (i.e., the label that historically correlates with better model F1 on validation set). We keep a tiny lookup for this.
4) If unsure after 90s, add a comment and route to pair-adjudication. Keep the adjudicator time budget per item to ~2 minutes.

Quick heuristics and shorthand for the adjudicator UI:
- "NORM" -> normalization only (punct/whitespace), no label change.
- "SPAN" -> adjust span boundaries only.
- "SPLIT" -> split into multiple entities (rare).
- "ESCALATE" -> pair-adjudication.
- "GZ" -> use gazetteer match.

Sampling notes and metrics we should monitor:
- Micro-adjudication throughput (items/day) per adjudicator. Target: 150/day.
- Escalation rate -> fraction sent to pair-adjudication. Target < 12%.
- Post-adjudication flip rate on validation -> how often model predictions revert after adjudication. Target < 3%.

Mini automation ideas (cheap wins):
- Regex bucket for obvious formatting fixes (emails, URLs, phone numbers) applied pre-adjudication.
- Majority-span normalizer: if two spans overlap >70% choose the intersection/union based on simple heuristics.
- Quick gazetteer matcher for ORG/PRODUCT with confidence score; only applied when gazetteer precision > 0.9 in last 90d.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent multi-label conflicts succinctly in the UI? (short tags vs full justification)
- Should we allow adjudicators to flag examples to add to training set? (Probably yes, but need storage workflow)
- Need a small experiment to measure adjudicator fatigue vs item complexity (A/B by complexity threshold).
- Build tiny metrics dashboard (Grafana) for throughput + escalation; talk to SRE about log paths.

Quick CLI snippets I drop into workspace when triaging: 
# grep for examples where majority labels disagree but spans equal
# (pseudo) python scripts/adjudication/query.py --disagree --span-eq --limit 50

Notes on language and tone: keep adjudication comments concise. Use explicit token offsets when necessary. When writing final Confluence page, convert heuristics into flowchart + examples.

Recent tickets to sync with: JIRA-7891 (micro-adjudication backlog), JIRA-8012 (gazetteer precision tuning). Slack thread: #labeling-ops (pinned messages re: adjudicator rotation).

Last quick log: tested majority-span normalizer on 1k examples, reduced escalations by ~7% but increased minor span-errors. Revert to intersection heuristic for hyphenated compounds.

-- End of scratchpad (Ava)
